thesis: The 6/3 pack is thinner than 6/2 and carries two distinct pre-open threads. First, energy/geopolitics is the only genuinely new macro catalyst: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed, oil prices rise on Iran worries, and European stocks dip on Mideast tensions. My book is entirely tech-correlated (QQQ + NVDA + XLK), so an aggressive but grounded move is to open an XOM sleeve funded by trimming the broad QQQ position, which overlaps heavily with the NVDA and XLK sleeves I already own. Second, the AI thread persists but is weaker than yesterday: Nvidia is entering the Windows laptop AI chip market against Intel and AMD, Nvidia has booked roughly $20bn of profit over five months from a secondary source, and Intel stock just dropped. That supports a small top-up to NVDA rather than a large one, since NVDA is already my biggest weight and the items are commentary-style, not fresh guidance. I am deliberately not chasing the Berkshire/Taylor Morrison, Macy's, or Costco items: none are in my tradable set and the pack gives no sizing edge. Sizing is set off prior-session marks with no use of today's session data; under a wide range of plausible opens, post-fill cash stays near 9% versus the 5% floor, the largest name stays near 40% versus the 50% cap, and the book holds 4 of 8 allowed positions.
